title: Using a fidget tool kindly
group: LDS-FOCUS — Focus and Getting Things Done
examples: Can a fidget help me listen?
How do I use a fidget at school?

explain.say: Some people listen better when their hands are busy. A fidget tool, like a squeeze ball, gives your hands a quiet job. Look at the board. You will sort ways to use a fidget.
The first group is lit up. It says kind and quiet. Squeeze it in your hand. Keep it low, under the desk. Twist it with no sound. Keep your eyes on the teacher. Can you squeeze your hand gently now?

Now look at the other group. It says pulls attention. Throwing it, loud clicking or playing a game with it. Then the fidget becomes a toy. Other people look at it instead of the lesson. Can you see the difference?
Here is a simple check. Ask yourself, Can I still hear the teacher? Ask, Are other people looking at my fidget? If you can hear, and others are working, you are using it kindly.
Sometimes a fidget starts to pull attention. Then put it in your pocket for a minute. That is a good choice. Today, tell a grown-up your 2 fidget rules. Keep it quiet, and keep it low.

faq.a: At school, a fidget is a tool. It keeps your hands busy so your brain can listen. When you play games with it, it becomes a toy.
asks: Tell me about Kind and quiet

faq.q: How does a fidget help me listen?
faq.a: Some people focus better when their hands are moving. The fidget gives the movement a quiet place to go.
It means your eyes, or other people's eyes, move to the fidget instead of the lesson. Throwing and clicking do that.

faq.q: Can I bring a fidget to school?
faq.a: Ask your teacher first. You can say, Would a fidget help me listen? A grown-up you trust can help you choose a quiet one.

faq.q: What other quiet fidgets are there?
faq.a: A smooth stone, a stretchy band, a bit of soft fabric, or putty. Quiet ones work best.

facts: A fidget tool is used to keep hands busy, while the eyes and ears stay on the lesson.
Quiet fidgets, like putty or a squeeze ball, are less distracting for others.

quiz.say: Sam has a fidget in class. Which way of using it is kind?
quiz.show: How can Sam use his fidget kindly?
quiz.why: Quiet squeezing keeps his hands busy, and everyone can still listen.

wrong.0: Throwing turns the fidget into a game, and people stop listening.
wrong.1: Loud clicks make other people look at the fidget.

quiz.say: Amira keeps looking at her fidget. She misses the lesson. What can she do?
quiz.show: Amira's fidget distracts her. What can she do?

options.show: Put it in her pocket for a minute
options.say: Put it in her pocket for a minute

options.show: Give it to a friend to throw
options.say: Give it to a friend to throw

quiz.why: A short pocket break helps her listen to the teacher again.

wrong.1: Playing more takes her eyes further from the lesson.
wrong.2: Throwing would make the whole class look at the fidget.
